# Short-recording loudnorm histogram regression

`loudnorm-histogram.wav` and `loudnorm-histogram.y4m` form a synthetic half-second
audio/video pair, generated by `scripts/generate_loudnorm_sample.py` without
FFmpeg, external encoders or private media. Audio is mono signed 16-bit PCM at
192 kHz, alternating +328/-328; video has 15 black/white 16x16 frames at 30 fps.

The newly implemented normalizer initially derived gain from exact accumulated
energy. Its reference behavior derives gain from 0.1 LU histogram bin centers.
This fixture distinguishes those decisions without resampling or codec errors.
The intended result is accepted by the public `apply_loudnorm` regression test;
it is not an unsupported-feature refusal test.

For a Nyquist square wave, the shelf magnitude is
`h = 10^(3.999843853973347/20)` and the high-pass magnitude is
`d = 1 + k/0.5003270373238773 + k²`, with
`k = tan(pi*38.13547087602444/192000)`. The weighted steady level is
`-0.691 + 20*log10((328/32768)*h*d) = -36.67185 LUFS`, well inside the
[-36.7, -36.6) bin. The independent expected gain for target -16 LUFS is
`10^((-16+36.65)/20)`, producing float32 samples of +/-0.10787577.

Ordinary tests read the checked-in files and invoke no generator or external
reference process. The explicit `ffmpeg_short_loudnorm_reference` benchmark
also compares this acceptance fixture with an external reference, separately
from the ordinary test suite.
